title.title: Maker builds Snaky in 21 moves
title.subtitle: Claim: on the empty infinite grid, Maker forces the Snaky hexomino within 21 of its own moves

plain: Two players take turns claiming squares: can one always build a six-square zigzag? Yes, in 21 moves

panels.caption: Snaky: six cells; any translation, rotation or reflection counts

panels.axisLabel: Maker moves, by certificate in the paper

beats.text: Snaky: the one hexomino whose Maker–Breaker game on the grid was undecided
Players alternately claim cells; Maker wins by owning a copy of Snaky
The claim: Maker wins within 21 moves, staying inside a fixed 251-cell region

steps: Start from positions where Maker completes Snaky at once
Combine claims so one Breaker reply can't spoil every option
Hundreds of combined claims build up to the empty board

achievement.label: Snaky in Harary's achievement game, open about 40 years
achievement.context: Known before: a winner in 3 dimensions and with a handicap, a loser on $8 \times 8$
achievement.note: A certificate of 728 conditions; it also works on a $17 \times 17$ board

verify.detail: An explicit Maker policy beats every legal Breaker sequence within 21 claims
verify.ourCheck: We read the Lean statement; we did not build it

voice.text: Players take turns claiming cells. Maker wants a copy of Snaky; Breaker blocks.
Winning positions are combined, step by step, until the empty board is one.
Claimed: Maker wins within twenty one moves.

sources.quote: within 21 Maker moves against any Breaker play; the strategy confines Maker to a fixed 251-cell region and works on a 17x17 board
an explicit certificate of 728 conditions; alternative 25- and 35-move certificates are also given
winner in 41 dimensions (Sieben, Integers 4 (2004) G05), in 3 dimensions and with planar handicap 1, loser on 8x8
holds a Snaky after 21 Maker claims
